suggestion_body: Instead of just stating what you did, quantify the impact. For example, 'Reduced API response time by 20%' or 'Scaled system to handle 10k concurrent users'.
Structure your bullet points using the STAR method: Situation, Task, Action, Result. Start with a strong action verb.
Hiring managers look for code samples. Make sure to include a link to your GitHub, GitLab, or Bitbucket profile.
Group your skills into categories like 'Languages', 'Frameworks', 'Databases', and 'DevOps Tools' for better readability.
Avoid rating your skills (e.g., 4/5 stars or 'Expert'). Instead, let your experience section demonstrate your proficiency level.
Clearly list the primary languages and frameworks used for each project (e.g., 'React, Node.js, MongoDB').
Highlight experience with CI/CD pipelines, Docker, Kubernetes, or cloud platforms like AWS/GCP to show you understand deployment.
If your project is hosted, provide a live demo URL alongside the repository link.
Mention your participation in Agile/Scrum ceremonies (sprints, standups) to show you fit into modern engineering workflows.
Keep programming languages separate from frameworks and libraries to avoid confusion (e.g., separate JavaScript and React).
Mention experience with unit testing, integration testing, TDD, or specific testing frameworks (e.g., Jest, JUnit, PyTest).
Include keywords related to code quality, such as code reviews, SOLID principles, linting, or SonarQube.
Ensure Git is explicitly mentioned in your skills section. It is a fundamental requirement for almost all dev roles.
Briefly explain why you built the project or the specific problem it solves, not just the technical 'how'.
If you mentored junior developers, led a squad, or onboarded new hires, explicitly mention it. Soft skills multiply tech skills.
Mention your focus on security, such as mitigating OWASP top 10 vulnerabilities, implementing OAuth, or handling PII securely.
Remove outdated technologies (e.g., Flash, SVN, older CMS platforms) unless explicitly required for the target role.
Highlight tasks involving database indexing, query optimization, or migrating between SQL/NoSQL to show deep data understanding.
Mention the architectural patterns used in your projects (e.g., Microservices, Event-Driven, MVC, Clean Architecture).
If you have given talks or written technical articles (Medium, Dev.to), include links to establish authority.
Specify the types of APIs you have built or integrated with (RESTful, GraphQL, gRPC).
Mention working directly with PMs, Designers, or QA to demonstrate your ability to function in a diverse product team.
Add cloud platforms (AWS, Azure, GCP) to your skills if you have experience with them, as they are highly searched keywords.
If you've contributed to open source, mention the specific repositories and the impact of your PRs.
In project descriptions, briefly mentioning a technical trade-off you navigated shows senior-level engineering maturity.
Mention experience with monitoring tools (Datadog, New Relic) and handling on-call rotations or resolving production incidents.
List the technologies you are most proficient with first within each category. ATS systems and recruiters scan left-to-right.
While teamwork is great, ensure your bullet points clearly state your specific individual contribution to the team's success.
Avoid listing Microsoft Office, Windows, or macOS as skills unless applying for IT Support. Focus on developer tools.
Highlight any manual processes you automated via scripts (Python, Bash) to show a proactive engineering mindset.
Mention significant third-party APIs you integrated (e.g., Stripe, Twilio, OAuth) as this is highly relevant to modern web dev.
Detail how you improved system performance, reduced memory leaks, or optimized frontend bundle sizes.
Instead of saying 'Familiar with Python', just list 'Python'. If you aren't comfortable being interviewed on it, leave it off.
Highlight instances where you refactored legacy code to improve maintainability or reduce technical debt.
List Linux/Unix if you are comfortable with the command line and server administration, as it's a huge plus for backend/DevOps.
Begin bullets with action verbs like Architected, Engineered, Developed, Deployed, or Spearheaded instead of 'Worked on'.
Instead of 'To-Do App', call it 'Task Management Dashboard'. It sounds more professional and impactful.
If you handled zero-downtime data migrations or schema updates at scale, feature this prominently.
If you have deep expertise in a major transition (e.g., Angular 14 vs AngularJS, React Hooks, Vue 3), specify it.
Ensure all GitHub, portfolio, and demo links are active and not returning 404 errors.
